issues.observed: The four KPI cards show only £2.44M, 42.1%, 109.6%, and 14, with no visible metric names, comparison periods, or status context.
issues.desired: Each card should be explicitly titled Total Revenue, Gross Margin, YoY Growth, and Risk Areas, with concise prior-period or target context where supported.
issues.action: Enable card category labels or add persistent titles above each value. Add prior-year variance or target context without changing the underlying measures, and use warning emphasis specifically for Risk Areas.

issues.observed: A prominent trial-capacity banner appears across the top of the deployed report.
issues.desired: The executive-facing report should open without licensing or trial notices.
issues.action: Deploy the report to appropriately licensed Power BI or Fabric capacity and validate the executive viewing experience in the intended production environment.

issues.observed: MonthName is not chronological; labels run through an irregular sequence such as April, August, December, February, January, July, and June. Several month labels are also truncated.
issues.desired: The trend should run in fiscal or calendar sequence so the CEO/CFO can interpret direction and seasonality correctly.
issues.action: Sort MonthName by a numeric fiscal-month index or use a YearMonth date field on a continuous axis. Preserve FiscalYear as the series only when multi-year comparison is analytically intended.

issues.observed: The Gross Margin trend uses the same nonchronological month ordering and heavily truncated labels, making the line shape analytically misleading.
issues.desired: Gross Margin % should be plotted in true temporal order with readable period labels.
issues.action: Apply the same fiscal-month sort column or YearMonth date axis used for the revenue trend and reduce label density rather than truncating most labels.

issues.observed: Total Revenue and YoY Growth % are displayed as clustered columns against a shared monetary scale. The percentage series collapses into an almost invisible line at zero.
issues.desired: Revenue magnitude and growth rate should both be clearly visible despite having different units and scales.
issues.action: Use Power BI's line and clustered column chart: revenue as columns on the primary currency axis and YoY Growth % as a line on the secondary percentage axis. Add growth labels and conditional red/green formatting where appropriate.

issues.observed: The category chart plots Total Revenue and YoY Growth % together on a monetary horizontal axis, so only revenue bars are meaningfully visible and category growth cannot be compared.
issues.desired: The chart should communicate both category revenue and category growth without mixing incompatible units on one scale.
issues.action: Keep revenue as sorted horizontal bars and expose YoY Growth % through a separate aligned growth visual, matrix column, or supported overlay/custom visual. If a custom visual is not permitted, use a matrix with data bars for revenue and conditionally formatted growth percentages.

issues.observed: Chart titles expose field names such as TotalRevenue, GrossMarginPct, YoYGrowthPct, MonthName, RegionName, and CategoryName.
issues.desired: Titles should use concise business language such as Revenue Trend, Gross Margin % Trend, Regional Performance, and Category Performance.
issues.action: Replace autogenerated titles and axis labels with executive-friendly display names. Hide redundant axis titles when the chart title and units already make the metric clear.

issues.observed: The value 109.6% is presented without a title or comparison definition. It is unusually large and therefore requires context, even if the measure is correct.
issues.desired: Executives should immediately understand whether this is YoY revenue growth, an index, or another percentage and which periods are being compared.
issues.action: Label the card YoY Growth and add a subtitle or tooltip identifying the current and comparison fiscal periods. Validate formatting and aggregation semantics, but do not alter the measure solely because the result is large.

issues.observed: The value 14 is visually indistinguishable from the positive KPIs and gives no indication of what constitutes a risk area.
issues.desired: Risk Areas should read as an exception KPI, with clear adverse status and access to the underlying drivers.
issues.action: Add the Risk Areas label, use restrained warning red when RiskCount is above the agreed threshold, and provide a tooltip or drill-through to the contributing regions/categories.

issues.observed: The slicers are positioned appropriately at the top, but their selected values appear partially clipped and use checkbox/list presentation inside very shallow containers.
issues.desired: Selected fiscal period, region, and category should be fully readable at a glance without scrolling within the slicer.
issues.action: Use compact dropdown slicers with sufficient height and visible selected-state text. Add a reset-filters control and confirm that selections are not obscured at the deployed viewport size.

issues.observed: There is no visible Executive Overview page title or reporting-period context. The page begins directly with slicers and unlabeled numbers.
issues.desired: A clear page title and current reporting context should establish hierarchy before the KPI row.
issues.action: Add an Executive Overview heading with a compact dynamic subtitle showing the active fiscal period and filter scope.

issues.observed: Gross Margin varies within a narrow range around 42%, but the small plot and dense labels make meaningful changes hard to assess.
issues.desired: The chart should make month-to-month movement visible while clearly communicating the percentage scale.
issues.action: Use a clean percentage axis with one-decimal formatting, fewer x-axis labels, and optional target/reference line. Avoid misleadingly tight scaling unless the axis limits remain clearly visible.

issues.observed: Green is used for revenue bars and the 2022 series, while red is used for 2023 and YoY Growth. This makes red and green alternate between time-series identity and positive/negative status meanings.
issues.desired: Colour should distinguish metric identity and status consistently, without implying that an entire year is good or bad.
issues.action: Use a neutral executive palette for years and revenue, reserving green and red for favorable and unfavorable variance. Check contrast and avoid relying on red/green alone.

issues.observed: Legends, axis labels, and category labels are very small relative to the canvas and would be difficult to read in a boardroom or shared-screen setting.
issues.desired: All essential labels should remain legible at normal report-view scale and when projected.
issues.action: Increase chart titles to approximately 14-16 px and essential labels to at least 10-12 px, subject to the final display size. Remove redundant labels to create room rather than shrinking text.

issues.observed: Category bars are not ordered by revenue or growth, weakening ranking and exception detection.
issues.desired: Categories should be ranked by the metric most relevant to executive comparison, normally Total Revenue, with growth exceptions still visible.
issues.action: Sort descending by Total Revenue by default and use growth formatting or labels to highlight underperformers.

issues.observed: Only London and Scotland are shown, and no indication explains whether this is the full regional scope or the result of active filters/data availability.
issues.desired: The scope of the regional comparison should be explicit so executives do not mistake a partial view for enterprise coverage.
issues.action: Show active filter context in the page subtitle or visual subtitle and verify whether all expected regions are represented. Do not fabricate or force-display regions that are absent from the data.

issues.observed: The page uses nearly uniform white containers on a pale background with limited grouping, weak borders, and little separation between executive KPIs and supporting analysis.
issues.desired: A restrained card system should establish KPI, trend, and breakdown sections while maintaining a clean enterprise aesthetic.
issues.action: Apply consistent card backgrounds, subtle borders or shadows, controlled corner radii, and standardized internal padding. Keep effects restrained and compatible with native Power BI formatting.

issues.observed: The major rows align reasonably well, but the unequal trend-panel widths and tight gutters make the page feel assembled rather than deliberately structured.
issues.desired: The layout should follow a repeatable grid with consistent gutters and balanced analytical weight.
issues.action: Use a consistent 4-column KPI grid and 2-column analytical grid, with uniform outer margins, gutters, and visual heights.

summary: The deployed page contains the required KPI, trend, regional, and category content, but it is not yet suitable for CEO/CFO use. The largest analytical problems are missing KPI labels, nonchronological month axes, and the use of shared scales for currency and percentage measures, which makes growth effectively unreadable. Technical field-name titles, clipped slicers, inconsistent colour semantics, weak exception storytelling, and the production trial banner further reduce credibility. Most visual and analytical presentation issues are achievable with native Power BI formatting, model sorting, combo charts, and a disciplined executive theme.
reference_rejected_ideas: Pixel-for-pixel reproduction of the Power BI service chrome, navigation rail, toolbar, and user controls is unnecessary because these are host-environment elements rather than report-page analytics.

The reference's horizontal revenue bars with independently scaled YoY dots may require a custom visual or layered workaround; a native matrix with data bars and a growth column is a more maintainable alternative when custom visuals are restricted.
Decorative KPI sparklines should not be added unless they use a consistent, correctly ordered time grain and provide information beyond the main trend charts.
Green and red should not automatically be copied from the reference for all positive and negative values without confirmed business polarity, thresholds, and accessibility treatment.
The reference date range, values, geographic labels, and category labels are illustrative and should not replace the deployed report's actual fiscal calendar, currency, or data scope.
